introH2: 🌊 What kinds of Bang Saray beach stays are there, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: Bang Saray and Na Jomtien are the quiet beaches south of Pattaya that Bangkokians have been quietly falling for — cleaner sand than central Pattaya, a fishing-village feel, fresh seafood at friendly prices, and a wider range of seaside stays than you'd expect. Some are private pool villas where you open the door, step into the pool, and keep walking down to the beach. Some are small boutique resorts where every room faces the sea, with a balcony for watching the sunset. And some are easy-on-the-wallet seaside hotels that suit families coming to splash around near the water park. The catch is that plenty of people book in this area without realising just how "quiet and far" it is from Walking Street, and the trip doesn't match what they pictured. This article gathers 9 beach stays in Bang Saray and Na Jomtien that we've already reviewed in depth, ranked from premium down to budget — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, with the upsides and the honest caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Bang Saray and Na Jomtien don't have a rail line or dense public transport — having your own car or being ready to use Grab is by far the easiest. It's about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok. The closest airport is U-Tapao (UTP), about a 20–30 min drive, ideal if you're flying in directly. The areas covered here: Bang Saray — a fishing village, quiet beach, fresh seafood, walking distance to the fishing pier and the sand. Na Jomtien — continues on from Bang Saray towards Pattaya, with private resort beaches and the same calm feel. Both areas are about a 25–45 min drive from central Pattaya and Walking Street — if you're set on a night out you'll need to budget for the ride and the time, but if you're here to unwind by a quiet sea, this is the right spot.

entries.name: U Pattaya (Bang Saray)
entries.revCount: TripAdvisor 4.6/5 · 1,213 reviews · #1 on Bang Saray beach
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Bang Saray beach · about 25–35 min to central Pattaya
entries.addr: 199/9 Moo 5, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Of all 9 Bang Saray beach stays we've reviewed, when it comes to luxury and privacy many reviews put U Pattaya (Bang Saray) out front — a 5-star beachfront boutique resort in the U Hotels & Resorts group, tucked along Bang Saray beach in Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District. It has just 44 keys, split into 25 rooms in the building and 19 villas, designed around a fishing-village concept in wood and bamboo tones. What makes people fall for it is the Beachfront Pool Villa, which sits right on the sand with a private pool of about 8 x 3 metres and a daybed — open the door from the living room, step into the pool, and walk straight down to the beach. Many guests say in their reviews that they wake up to the sea every morning, and it's so quiet it feels like a different world from Pattaya. The shared area has an infinity pool that runs out towards Bang Saray bay, a popular photo spot in the late afternoon, plus a U Spa, a rooftop bar, and the group's 24-hour stay clock that counts a full day from whatever time you check in, with breakfast you can have anywhere, any time, per the U group concept. Service draws consistent praise because the resort is small, guests are few, and staff look after you closely enough that it feels personal — which is why it holds #1 of the 8 hotels in Bang Saray on TripAdvisor, scoring 4.6 out of 5 from 1,213 reviews. The honest caveats from the reviews: the location is fairly far and quiet, with no shops or malls within walking distance, so you'll lean on a car every time you head out; food prices at the resort run high for the quality; and being a seaside resort, some of the woodwork is starting to show its age and the effects of humidity. This isn't the best value per baht, but it's the best choice for honeymooning couples and families who want a private seaside pool villa in a calm setting, escaping the bustle of Pattaya for a bit of slow living.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're set on a beachfront pool villa, book ahead and specify the Beachfront Pool Villa clearly — there are only a few and they fill fast on holidays. Budget for resort food, or drive out for fresh seafood at Bang Saray market for some meals, and confirm the minibar list clearly at check-in.

entries.addr: 78/4 Moo 8, Sukhumvit Road KM.163, Na Jomtien, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Just a hair behind U Pattaya on score, Sea Sand Sun Resort and Villas is a 5-star private-beach resort tucked into the Na Jomtien area near Bang Saray, and it's the place that holds #1 of the 30 hotels in Na Jomtien on TripAdvisor with 4.8 out of 5, plus a 9.1 from 136 reviews on Trip.com. What sets it apart is how its roughly 60 rooms and villas are laid out in a green, shady Bali-style garden right beside a private white-sand beach where the water is clear and the crowds are thin — a rarity in the Pattaya area. The beach has canvas loungers and free kayaks to paddle. Rooms range from Boutique Garden Room and Garden Villa at about 55 sqm, up to the 120 sqm Deluxe Pavilion Villa and the top Pool Villa Suite of around 200 sqm with a full private pool. Plenty of reviews use the word "immaculate" for the cleanliness, and call the staff's service "the best part of all," with many guests returning for a third or fourth stay. Another thing that makes it special is its pet-friendly policy — you can bring your dog, which is rare for a luxe beachfront resort. The shared area has a free-form pool in the garden, a kids' pool, an outdoor jacuzzi, and Sea Sand Sun Spa. The honest caveats from the reviews: the location is about 15 km, or a 40–45 min drive, from central Pattaya and Walking Street, which isn't convenient if you're set on a night out — you'll mainly rent a car or use Grab; resort food and spa prices run fairly high; the kids' menu has few options; and some rooms face the garden more than the sea. It suits couples and families best (including those bringing the dog) who want to escape the bustle for a calm private beach, treating the resort itself as the destination of the trip rather than a base for heading out every day.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If sea views matter to you, ask for an Ocean View room or a villa near the beach at the time of booking, since some rooms face the garden. Budget for resort food, or head out for fresh seafood in Bang Saray village to mix it up, and if you're bringing a pet, confirm the terms with the resort ahead of time.

entries.name: Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya
entries.revCount: Real reviews around 9.1 · thousands of guests
entries.badge: 🌊 Every room has a sea view · lots of reviews
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Bang Saray beach · about 25 min to Pattaya city
tags: 🌊 Every room has a sea view
entries.addr: 4/2 Moo 5, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: If you want that Bang Saray seaside feel without paying 5-star money, Kept Bangsaray Hotel Pattaya is the option reviews mention most often in the 4-star group — a small seaside boutique resort of about 27 rooms in the Bang Saray area, Sattahip District, open since around 2017, and a place with thousands of guest reviews; its real-review score sits at about 9.1. The selling point every review agrees on is that every room faces the sea with a private balcony — no rooms looking at a wall or a car park. Open the balcony door in the morning and there's Bang Saray's sea with small fishing boats drifting in the distance. The design is a coastal style that borrows the feel of the Bang Saray fishing village; rooms range from the Kept Suite for couples and the Kept Family Suite for families, up to the two-storey Kept Skyline Duplex with wide sea views from the upper floor. The shared area has a seaside pool and a fishing pier reaching out into the water for squid jigging in the evening, plus free bikes to borrow around the village and a seaside restaurant. The location is considered closer to Pattaya city than many resorts in this area, about a 25 min drive. The honest caveats: it's a small resort, so the facilities aren't as extensive as a big one; the surroundings are quiet and you'll need a car to head out; and it suits people coming to unwind by the sea more than those after lively activities. Overall it's the sweet spot for anyone who wants a sea-view room on Bang Saray beach at a lighter price than a pool villa, while still getting the full quiet, scenic feel.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Every room does have a sea view, but some get a more open one. Read the latest room photos in reviews and ask for a room with an unobstructed view before booking. In the evening, head out for squid jigging on the fishing pier, and take the free bikes into the village to find fresh seafood at friendly prices.

entries.type: Boutique Residence 3-Star · Walk to the Beach
entries.name: Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Saray · walk to Bang Saray beach · about 400 m from the fishing pier
entries.addr: 48/8-9 Moo 4, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Switching from the premium tier to the easy-on-the-wallet, good-value group, Baan Pimpisa Bangsaray Boutique Residence is a small 3-star boutique residence of just 16 rooms in the Bang Saray area, with prices starting at only about ฿1,100/night — yet real reviews credit it for its calm, its cleanliness, and warm staff, earning about 8.8 from 220 reviews on Trip.com. Its charm is the colonial-style building with a koi pond in the middle of the garden, giving it the feel of staying at a small guesthouse rather than a hotel. Open since 2015, it has two pools (indoor and outdoor), a kids' pool, a BBQ corner, bikes to borrow, and free private parking. The rooms are Superiors decorated in a warm, homey style, with air-con, fridge, TV, safe, free Wi-Fi, and some have a balcony or terrace overlooking the garden and pool. The location is about 400 metres from the Bang Saray fishing pier, and Bang Saray beach is within walking distance — more convenient than many resorts that need a car. The honest caveats from the reviews: it's a small place with no lift; there's some sound carry between rooms; the Bang Saray area has sparse public transport, so you'll want your own car if you'll head into Pattaya city often; and the facilities are simple, in line with the price. It suits couples and travellers best who want a calm seaside feel in Bang Saray, within walking distance of the beach, on the most accessible budget in the boutique group of this article.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The building has no lift and reviews mention sound carry between rooms, so if you sleep lightly or have heavy luggage, ask for a corner or ground-floor room when you book. The star of the area is the fresh seafood by Bang Saray beach within walking distance — fresher and friendlier on price than in Pattaya city.

entries.name: Sunset Park Resort and Spa
entries.badge: 🌴 Private beach · cottages in the woods
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien–Bang Saray · about 30 min to Pattaya city
entries.addr: 99/19 Moo 3, Soi Na Jomtien 48, Sukhumvit Road, Na Jomtien, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: If you prefer a "nature and quiet" feel over luxury, Sunset Park Resort and Spa is a beachfront cottage resort in the Na Jomtien-into-Bang Saray area that leans into this clearly — about 53 wooden cottages spread through dense green woods by the beach, with a stream and small waterfalls running through. The biggest draw is a private sandy beach about 206 metres long and a seaside infinity pool a few steps from your room. Open since 2003 and improved continuously, it scores about 8.4 from 128 reviews on Trip.com. Rooms range from the Brook Side Cottage by the stream in the woods, the Bay View Cottage facing the bay with sea views, up to the Beach Spa Villa for those who want a newer room. There are two pools, a full-service spa, a sauna, and a beachfront dining room. To be honest, as the reviews reflect: because it's a resort that's been open more than 20 years, some of the wooden cottages are old with age, so it's worth choosing a recently renovated room and checking the latest room photos in reviews before booking. The location is about 30 min from town, too far to walk anywhere, so you'll need a car; and because it sits in the woods near a stream, there are bugs and mosquitoes as a matter of course, especially in the evening and the rainy season, so pack repellent. It suits people best who are after a beachfront cottage feel amid nature, trading a brand-new room for a private beach and quiet on a budget of about ฿2,500.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some wooden cottages are old with age — ask for a Spa Suite or Beach Spa Villa, which are in better shape, and check the latest room photos in reviews before booking. The resort sits in the woods near a stream, so bring mosquito repellent, especially in the evening and the rainy season.

entries.name: The Sunset Village

entries.addr: 89/5 Soi Na Jomtien 52, Sukhumvit Road KM.162.5, Na Jomtien, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Close to Sunset Park in both location and concept, The Sunset Village (full name Sunset Village Beach Resort) is a Thai-style beachfront cottage resort tucked into the Na Jomtien–Bang Saray area, south of Pattaya. It's a long-standing resort, open since 1991 and renovated in 2017, with about 61 cottages and rooms spread across spacious seaside grounds, decorated in a Thai style with wood and bamboo. What many people mention is the calm, the private beach, and the shady seaside-village feel that's hard to find in Pattaya — walk out of your cottage through the green garden to sip a drink by the pool, where the far end opens onto the Na Jomtien sea. There are two outdoor pools, one of them a seaside pool next to the restaurant, plus a kids' pool, a sauna, a jacuzzi, a Thai massage spa, and the Sea Terrace beachfront restaurant. Rooms range from the Deluxe Beach Room and Premium Beach Bungalow by the beach, up to the Garden Pool Villa for those who want a private pool. The location is about a 15 min walk to Bang Saray beach and the Columbia Pictures Aquaverse water park, with SHA Plus certification and a review score of about 8.2 out of 10. The honest caveats from the reviews: there are no shops or malls within walking distance of the resort, so you'll need a car and should plan to buy essentials beforehand; being in a garden of trees by the sea, there may be mosquitoes or bugs in some seasons; and with cottages spread across several zones, some get a sea view while others face the garden. It suits people who want a Thai-style wooden cottage feel by the sea, with spacious, calm grounds, bringing the family for a stay near the water park on a budget of about ฿2,500.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The cottages are spread across several zones, so if you want a sea view and the sunset, specify a beachfront room or one near the seaside pool at the time of booking. Bring mosquito repellent and essentials beforehand, since there are no shops within walking distance of the resort.

tags: 🌊 Every room has a sea view
entries.addr: 75 Moo 4, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Among the easy-on-the-wallet seaside stays in Bang Saray, when it comes to a romantic mood, Baan Tah On The Sea is the one reviews mention often — a small 3-star seaside resort in the Bang Saray area, about 24–33 rooms and villas, open since 2013 and renovated in 2023, scoring about 8.6 from 528 reviews across Trip.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor. The standout every review agrees on is that every room faces the sea with a sea view, and many have a balcony with a daybed for watching the sunset — wake up and open the door to the sea filling the view, and in the evening head down to sip a drink at the waterside lounge as the sun sinks behind Bang Saray bay. Rooms range from the Deluxe Seaview at about 35 sqm, which starts at just ฿1,200 on weekdays, the Studio Seaview with glass walls and a panoramic view plus a bathtub, up to the Family Room Seaview at about 80 sqm for families. There's a seaside restaurant/cafe, a waterside lounge corner with hammocks, a BBQ corner, bikes to borrow, an EV charging point, and activities like squid jigging, fishing, and kayaking. The location is about 660 metres from the Bang Saray fishing pier, with Bang Saray beach within walking distance. The honest caveats from the reviews: not every room gets the same view — ground-floor rooms near the fishing pier tend to get a more open one, while some second-floor Studios get a view of the bay's curve — and some reviews mention uneven cleanliness in certain rooms, so read the latest reviews and check the room at check-in. It suits couples best who want a romantic seaside mood, watching the sunset on a light budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Not every room gets the same view — ground-floor rooms near the fishing pier tend to get a more open sea view, so ask and pick your room when you book. Check the cleanliness when you enter the room and ask to switch right away if it isn't right, and try buying fresh seafood from Bang Saray market to grill at the BBQ corner.

entries.name: Costa Well Resort - Jacuzzi Wing
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Jomtien 56 · walk to Bang Saray beach · about 20–25 min to town
entries.addr: 555 Soi Na Jomtien 56, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: If you want a stay that's "photogenic" and has an in-room jacuzzi on a modest budget, Costa Well Resort Pattaya - Jacuzzi Wing is an interesting option in the Na Jomtien 56 area on the Bang Saray side — a Mediterranean-style boutique resort that plays on a Greek Santorini theme in white and blue against blue domes, which has become a popular photo spot for this zone. The selling point of this wing is its rooms with a private jacuzzi tub on the balcony, plus two rooftop saltwater pools looking out over the Bang Saray sea, at their best around sunset. Open in 2017 and improved in 2022, it's a condotel building with several room types, from the Deluxe with jacuzzi from about ฿1,500, up to the Deluxe Ocean View + Jacuzzi and the One-Bedroom Suite. The location is about 20–25 min from Pattaya town, with Bang Saray beach a few minutes' walk away. To be honest, as the reviews reflect: the score sits at about 7.7, lower than the others in this article, because there are caveats around upkeep — jacuzzi tub condition varies room to room, some reviews report discoloured water in certain rooms, and being a condotel, room management is less consistent than a centrally run hotel. Good on design and price, but ask for a room with a jacuzzi in good shape, test the water at check-in, and pick a higher floor for the sea view. It suits photo-minded couples who want an in-room jacuzzi and a Greek mood on a light budget, with upkeep expectations set accordingly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Jacuzzi tub condition varies room to room — specify a room with a tub in good shape and ask to see the room before check-in if you can. Some reviews report discoloured water in certain rooms, so run the water to test at check-in, and pick a higher floor for a better sea view.

entries.name: The Wind Hotel Pattaya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Saray–Na Jomtien · walk to the beach · near Aquaverse ~1.7 km
entries.addr: 88/8 Moo 8, Soi Na Jomtien 56/1, Bang Saray Subdistrict, Sattahip District
entries.storyHtml: Closing the article with the most budget-friendly option, The Wind Hotel Pattaya is a mid-size hotel of about 140 rooms in the Bang Saray-Na Jomtien area, whose clear selling point is a very light price for a seaside hotel, starting at about ฿900–1,100/night in normal periods, and it's the place with the most guest reviews in this article, at about 2,703; its real-review score sits at about 7.8. Open since 2013, it has an indoor saltwater pool, a restaurant, a bar, a massage room, a billiard room, bikes to borrow, and free parking; many rooms have a balcony and some see the sea. What makes it especially good for families is its location near the Columbia Pictures Aquaverse water park, only about 1.7 kilometres away, making it easy to bring the kids to splash around; drive about two hours from Bangkok, park free at the hotel, and walk a few hundred metres to Bang Saray beach. Rooms range from the Basic Standard from ฿900, the Basic With Balcony, up to the Basic Sea View that sees the sea. To be honest, as the reviews reflect: this is a budget hotel, not a luxe resort — the rooms are simple and not every room sees the sea, and some reviews mention bugs in the room, so it's worth checking the room at check-in and keeping food sealed away. It suits family trips best, bringing the kids to splash at Aquaverse, and anyone who wants a Bang Saray seaside stay on the lightest budget, with expectations set mainly on value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Not every room sees the sea, so if you want a view, specify a Basic Sea View room from the start. Check the room at check-in and keep food sealed away, and compare stay-plus-ticket packages for the nearby Aquaverse water park, about 1.7 km away, before booking.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers ask most about Bang Saray beach stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Bang Saray beach stay?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget. For luxury and a beachfront pool villa, U Pattaya (Bang Saray), scoring 9.2, holds #1 on Bang Saray beach on TripAdvisor. For a quiet private beach where you can bring a pet, Sea Sand Sun is #1 in Na Jomtien. For a sea view in every room at a lighter price, Kept Bangsaray. And for the budget-minded, Baan Tah On The Sea at ฿1,200 and Baan Pimpisa at ฿1,100 are great value.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Bang Saray stays cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿900–4,000 per night. The most budget-friendly is The Wind Hotel from ฿900 · Baan Pimpisa ฿1,100 · Baan Tah ฿1,200 · Costa Well ฿1,500 · mid-range is Sunset Park and The Sunset Village ฿2,500 and Kept ฿2,900 · and the premium tier is U Pattaya and Sea Sand Sun from ฿4,000 (beachfront pool villa rooms up to about ฿12,000–15,000). All prices are approximate starting prices from a standard room; during long holidays prices may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Is Bang Saray far from Pattaya, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Bang Saray and Na Jomtien are south of Pattaya, about a 25–45 min drive from central Pattaya and Walking Street depending on each stay's location — Bang Saray is a touch closer to town than Na Jomtien. Public transport is sparse in this area, so having your own car or being ready to use Grab is the easiest. It's about a 2-hour drive from Bangkok. The closest airport is U-Tapao (UTP), about a 20–30 min drive.

faq.q: ❓ Which Bang Saray stay suits a family bringing kids to splash around?
faq.a: If you're bringing the kids to the water park, The Wind Hotel Pattaya is near Columbia Pictures Aquaverse, only about 1.7 km, on a light budget of around ฿900. If you want spacious grounds and a seaside pool, The Sunset Village has wooden cottages on spacious grounds with two pools. And for families who want a private pool villa so the kids can splash with peace of mind, U Pattaya and Sea Sand Sun have Pool Villas and separate kids' pools.

faq.q: ❓ Does Bang Saray have private beachfront pool villas?
faq.a: Yes. U Pattaya (Bang Saray) has a Beachfront Pool Villa right on the sand with a private pool of about 8x3 metres, from around ฿12,000 · Sea Sand Sun has a Pool Villa Suite of about 200 sqm with a private pool. And for those who want a private pool on a lighter budget, The Sunset Village has a Garden Pool Villa from about ฿5,500, and Costa Well has a private in-room jacuzzi from about ฿1,500.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book a Bang Saray stay?
faq.a: Most Bang Saray beach stays are small resorts (16–60 rooms, some just 27), so they fill fast, especially the pool villas and sea-view rooms. For long holidays and high season, book 3–4 weeks ahead or more, especially U Pattaya and Sea Sand Sun. For ordinary weekdays, 1–2 weeks is enough. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in a price like that first if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best rate.
